name: ticketing
description: Events and venues with seat maps, expiring seat holds, checkout with price tiers and discount codes, refunds and a sales report.
author: test2 benchmark author (Claude subagent)

issues.description: The docstring promises rounding to the nearest cent but int() truncates, so a discounted 1995 at 15% gives 1695 instead of 1696.
issues.fix_hint: Round the discounted amount (round() or integer half-up arithmetic) instead of truncating with int().

issues.description: Revenue is documented as what customers paid after discounts, but the report adds the undiscounted tier price.
max_uses is the total number of orders allowed, but the check only refuses once times_used exceeds it, so the code can be redeemed max_uses + 1 times.
Ticket codes admit the holder at the gate but are drawn from the seedable Mersenne Twister in the random module, so they can be predicted.
issues.fix_hint: Draw the code from a cryptographic source (secrets or random.SystemRandom).

issues.description: purchase imports refunds for the refund deadline and refunds imports purchase for TicketOffice, so the two modules depend on each other.

issues.description: The two CSV exports repeat the same buffer, writer, encode, write and checksum steps; only the header and row values differ.
cancel_event nests loops and conditions five levels deep (for, if, for, if, plus an if/else accumulator) where early continues and dict.get would keep it flat.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: MD5 is only an integrity checksum for export files, declared not for security; nothing relies on collision resistance.
It iterates over a list copy of the items, so deleting from the dict inside the loop is safe.
